The five names are the strongest evidence for that scenario, so they go in with each cause quoted exactly and Draft and Penflip marked cause unverified. Upsource's stated cause bites hardest: standalone review tools lose to review inside the tool people already use. That points at the surface decision, and Q3 answers it with one web surface first and the Mac app later from the same tree, so the pitch has to say why a standalone editor survives where Upsource did not. The files agents obey have no tool today, so there is nothing to lose to. If the twenty conversations show teams buying a standalone review surface, this becomes a footnote.

questions.recWhy: Regulated software teams keeping quality documents as markdown in git are the only adjacent buyer already on our substrate, which is true of no other buyer with a budget. Nothing opened requires what we sell: MHRA permits audit trails reviewed by exception, the EMA's 2024 reflection paper is non-binding and names no granularity, pharma mandates whole-document approval and aviation a per-page revision date. The blocker is sales cost, SOC 2 and a nine to eighteen month cycle, and Q13 leaves enterprise unpriced until somebody asks. So design for them, which mostly means never destroying a review record, and chase the buyer Q2 names. The caveat in (b) is written on the card because designing for a buyer nobody talked to is exactly what produced two features validated on the wrong person. Two or more of the twenty conversations landing on regulated teams already in git makes (a) the segment.
